title: P01 fixed-depth looped transformer: three unique Peri-LN blocks applied twice (A-B-C-A-B-C), six logical applications as before, on the 115-fable hybrid ALiBi/NoPE Lean incumbent (2,427,648 params)
description: Idea ID: P01 (fixed-depth loop, Robbie's pick). The six untied blocks become three unique blocks cycled twice, A-B-C-A-B-C: the same six logical applications, FLOPs and step rate as 115, with 2,427,648 unique parameters instead of 4,800,000. 105-claude confounded sharing with an extra seventh application (which cost steps and matched the untied 102) and 106-claude shared only attention across all six blocks; this isolates full-block weight reuse at fixed depth and zero systems cost, so a reused block must learn one general extend-the-proof-state operator rather than six depth-specialised ones, which should transfer better to the longer chains expert iteration asks for.
hypothesis: Pretraining is data-limited (115: 3.5 epochs, val loss flat at ~0.083 from 165 s while train loss falls to 0.049), so the incumbent spends its second half memorising cap-6 proofs in depth-specific weights. Proof extension is an iterated operation (each Lean line applies one rule to earlier lines), so a block reused at two depths is pushed toward a general, position-in-depth-agnostic inference-step circuit instead of memorised depth-specific lookups; the halved parameter count also removes memorisation capacity without removing depth or attention machinery (the ALiBi/NoPE gains). Expert iteration should then find a starting point that generalises to 7+ lines at least as well, and its 600-step AdamW rounds adapt a 2.4M model as fast as a 4.8M one. Prediction if right: steps within 3% of 115 (4,100-4,300), final val loss 0.083-0.090 with a smaller train/val gap (train >= 0.055), held-out greedy >= 0.975, round-1 targets solved >= 690 (115: 718/756/691), 3-seed mean above 631.33. Evidence against: 106 (shared attention, 3.48M) lost 23 and 105 lost 34, and pre-Lean sharing runs lost; if the six depths genuinely need different operators (parse hypotheses early, cite and emit late), a shared block underfits and val loss > 0.092 with round-1 targets < 650 and a loss of 20-50. Mechanism checks: steps vs 115; train/val gap; round-1 targets solved and sample acc; round-1 Lean parse failures; eval L* and >= 10 histogram vs 115.
expected_delta: -45 to +40 theorems at >=7 (central +3); pretraining 4,100-4,300 steps (115: 4,204/4,218/4,263), final val loss 0.083-0.090, held-out greedy >= 0.975, total_secs ~2,050-2,200

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 115, CHANGED: P01 fixed-depth looped transformer, three unique blocks applied in a cycle A-B-C-A-B-C
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (CHANGED from 113's all-ALiBi): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: model.blocks = ModuleList(unique * 2) where unique = 3 PeriLNBlocks, so blocks[i] is blocks[i+3]. Every logical application (attention with the same hybrid ALiBi/NoPE bias, Peri-LN, GELU MLP) is byte-identical to 115; only which weights each depth uses changed. Same six sequential block applications per token, so FLOPs, activation memory and step rate match 115 (no extra logical block as in 105-claude, no attention-only sharing as in 106-claude). Gradients of a shared block sum over its two applications (autograd); Muon momentum buffers and Newton-Schulz run once per unique matrix. Width, heads, GELU, untied embedding/readout, ln_f, init (orthogonal on the 12 unique block matrices), optimizer and schedule unchanged
arch.n_params_detail: 3 unique blocks x 790,784 (qkv 197,376 + proj 65,792 + fc1 263,168 + fc2 262,400 + 4 LayerNorms 2,048) = 2,372,352 + emb 27,392 + head 27,392 + ln_f 512 = 2,427,648 (vocab 107); the fork's n_params() and the harness sum self.parameters(), which dedupe the aliased blocks (checked on CPU: both 2,427,648). 115: 4,800,000
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py, replace blocks with ModuleList([A, B, C, A, B, C]) of PeriLNBlocks, then load state (state_dict keys blocks.0-5 exist, blocks.3-5 alias blocks.0-2). Loading into six untied blocks gives the same function only if blocks 3-5 receive the same tensors as 0-2. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: unchanged fork code: sample.generate builds one cache dict per model.blocks entry, so six distinct caches, one per logical application (same aliasing as 105-claude, which ran cleanly). CPU check with the pinned fork 51604b3: 2-sequence prefill of 8 tokens plus 4 cached one-token steps vs the full forward, max abs logit diff 7.2e-7; loss/backward run; 2,427,648 params
arch.n_layers_detail: 6 logical applications of 3 unique blocks (A-B-C-A-B-C); N_LAYER = 6, N_UNIQUE = 3

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: CHANGED count: 12 unique hidden matrices (3 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight = 13 Muon matrices (115: 25); each shared matrix gets one momentum buffer and one orthogonalized update from the summed gradient of its two applications
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters of the 3 unique blocks (ln1, ln2, ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out) and ln_f; deduplicated by parameters()
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: CHANGED count: 12 unique hidden matrices (3 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight = 13 Muon matrices (115: 25); each shared matrix gets one momentum buffer and one orthogonalized update from the summed gradient of its two applications

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1. CHANGED: only 3 unique blocks are constructed and orthogonally initialised, so RNG draws differ from 115
